Lelanàn (L36)

Survey-region classification: Sarhal.

In brief: Beginning as a shrine-state devoted to Lel, Lelanàn turns love stories, perfume trade, and public relief into a way of governing—and ultimately challenges the magical boundaries of life and fertility.

Story: High | Mission-tree length: Medium (25 direct L36 missions) | Mission-tree update: Based on the current local Mod, supporting EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: Very high | Tedium: Medium (Love, province rituals, and magical projects require management) | Early pressure: Low to moderate | Expansion: Moderate (regional objectives share the focus with diplomacy and trade)

How a Shrine Became a State

This entry uses Lelanàn (L36) for the country shown as 丰水城 in the project Chinese localisation. It already existed in 1444; it is not a country formed later by the player. Its country history defines it as an Amezatany Halfling theocracy following the Nakavy Avo faith, with the Holy Matriarchy reform. Its capital, province 6599, belongs to L36 and contains Lel's temple, a holy site, a center of trade, and a fort. The opening ruler, Rangita Tallfriend, historically took office in 1408; she did not first come to power in 1444. Nearby Jakannakazy is set as a rival. These are local Mod starting conditions, not achievements from completing the mission tree.

Its national identity rests on devotion to Lel and a religious community of her daughters, priestesses, and guardians. An official developer diary places Rangita, Kyola Heartblade, and the Daughters of Lel at the center of the story, showing the creators' intended positive romance narrative; implementation and concrete effects remain a matter for the scripts. The offline English Wiki has no readable dedicated Lelanàn country page: it lists “Shrine of Lelanán” only in a list of historical countries and mentions Ixora perfume from Lelanàn in an expedition article. The former does not establish the 1444 government, and the latter proves neither the scale of trade nor an exact date. This article does not use these scattered references to invent a founding history.

Love Is More Than a Slogan

Lelanàn's unique government mechanic makes “Love” a resource that can be accumulated and spent. Missions, religion, and domestic circumstances affect its cycle; high Love is also linked to religious tolerance and reform progress. The player can spend it to relieve disaster-struck provinces, hold festivals of love, or strengthen Lel's paladins and marines. After completing missions associated with “The Labor of Love,” the player can also hire Daughters of Lel mercenaries, who can spend Love in their station city on long-term provincial development. This turns the story's theme into an operational loop: decide whether to spend a finite resource on relief, local stability, or saving up for the next major ritual.

Another strand begins with Ixora, a white flower, and the perfume trade. Early missions ask the player to develop the capital and flower fields, using plant-growth magic to increase output; only later do scent, trading posts, and stories from distant lands become an international network. Love in Lelanàn is not limited to courtship: missions and events also advance relationships across cultures and peoples, allowing more groups to find a place in the same society. A player post describes this aspect vividly, while also complaining about the micromanagement of moving mercenaries, checking province modifiers, and triggering rituals. That is a version-specific player experience from 2026, not a conclusion about current balance.

The Political Cost and Future of the City of Love

The 25 direct L36 missions form a medium-length campaign linking local reconstruction, the stories of Rangita and Kyola, the broken “City Marriage,” Lel's place in the pantheon, the lost Anánoma, and the telling of Halann's love stories abroad. Whether Kyola personally takes part in battle and whether she survives affect parts of the narrative; no single outcome should be written as established history in 1444. The late-game “Gift of Sharing Life” is a distinctive magical project: the player first develops cities, builds a mage tower and magical infrastructure, and then advances research into life and fertility through a multi-stage project. This is a future objective, not an ability available at the start.

The route has a clear tension. Relief for disaster victims, healing enemy wounded, inclusion across peoples, and improving reproductive choice are concrete positive actions. At the same time, the missions further concentrate Lel's primacy and priestly authority, limiting the scope for other Nakavy Avo gods to rise. Theocracy itself is not evil, and religious monopoly does not erase the aid given to people; these belong separately under “power structure” and “conduct.” Players seeking a fully secular, religiously permissive system will not find it here.

The current Mod also has a general decision to form Fahvanosy (S71), and L36 is not excluded. But the decision's comment explicitly says it does not automatically switch to another mission tree, while the display conditions for all five Lelanàn-specific mission groups require the current Tag to be L36. Therefore, forming S71 is not a verified continuation of Lelanàn's missions. This entry describes a route that keeps L36 and completes its own story; the missions displayed after formation and any inheritance effects have not been tested in play.

Personality and Recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 58/100 | Autocracy 76/100 | Magic–Artifice 94/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 90/100) | Pluralism 86/100. The phase profile shifts from Lel's shrine and perfume trade (Expansion 45, Magic–Artifice intensity 57) to divine primacy, the holy city, and life magic (Expansion 62, Magic–Artifice intensity 95).

The v2.1 values rating is Good (88/100), with a stable trajectory. Relief for disaster victims, healing the wounded, recognition of cross-cultural and non-traditional intimate relationships, and a commitment to sharing reproductive choice support dignity, public good, and personhood. Lel's supremacy and concentrated religious authority constrain pluralism and restraint, but neither theocracy nor war is itself a basis for a moral penalty. The weighted score is 88.3, rounded to 88.

Recommended for players who enjoy warm but not naïve character stories, religion and magic, provincial development, and a distinctive resource cycle. If you only want rapid conquest, dislike repeatedly managing provincial rituals, or expect the country to begin with its endgame magic, this campaign will not suit you.

The detailed boundaries for the offline Wiki, related official diary, and player posts are in the Chinese-source evidence page.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces current national traditions, seven national ideas and ambition. Traditions apply on adoption, ideas unlock through investment, and ambition follows completion of all seven. Only national ideas are listed, not racial, governmental or mission bonuses; predecessor and successor sets do not stack. Idea descriptions can recall history or describe future ideals and do not automatically establish events before 1444.

Effect displays and units are inherited for source parity, not independently certified; uncertain percentages remain accompanied by script keys and raw values.

Lelanàn Traditions

  • Diplomatic reputation: +100% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 1).

  • Diplomats: +1 (diplomats; raw value 1).

1. The Sisterhood

The devout of the Summer Isles followed the Avo Nakavy, or "Great Family," a pantheon of gods with associated domains and affinities not unlike those of the Regent Court. Like their Cannorian cousins, the followers of the Avo Nakavy disagreed over who should be considered the head of the pantheon - but not the rulers of Lelanàn, whose very state bore the name of the goddess "Lel" and venerated her as the head of the pantheon.

The goddess of Life, Love, and Water - the most essential elements of existence, Lel held an important spiritual and temporal role in Lelanàn. The rulers of Lelanàn hailed from an ancient order of priestesses known as the "the Sisterhood of Lel," who originally specialized in rites of fertility and conception. The popularity and importance of these rites allowed the Sisterhood to expand its duties to include those traditionally covered by some of the related gods - and soon, the Sisterhood was training its "Nakazy," or lesser priests specializing in funerary rites and rituals of the other Avo Nakavy, and adopting associated functions of the state. With time, the Sisterhood began to be recognized as the ruling elite in Lelanàn, and its high priestess, the Chosen of Lel, recognized as its highest authority.

  • Devotion: +1 (devotion; raw value 1).

  • Legitimacy: +1 (legitimacy; raw value 1).

  • Republican tradition: +0.3 (republican_tradition; raw value 0.3).

  • Horde unity: +1 (horde_unity; raw value 1).

2. Temporal Authority

While Lel’s leadership over the Avo Nakavy was recognized in Lelanàn, the rest of the Summer Isles suffered from discord over the relative position of the gods within the pantheon. The migration of humans into Vyzemby’s coastal cities, areas where Kolo’s followers had the greatest sway, and disarray among his followers and other rival claimants left the Sisterhood in an advantageous position to advance their own interpretation of the faith.

In a series of religious edicts and interpretations by the Chosen of Lel herself, the Sisterhood asserted the primacy of Lel as the clear leader of the pantheon. Kolo claimed dominion over the earth and the abundance of food it brings - but what good was the earth without water and life to bring this abundance into existence? How could Yuye claim dominion over storms alone, when Lel gave the Vyzemby the gift of water? It was through this logic that Lel was reinforced as the clear head of the pantheon among the Sisterhood and its followers.

  • Clergy loyalty equilibrium: +10% (church_loyalty_modifier; raw value 0.1).

3. A Modern Anánoma

Once a sleepy temple town on the northern coast, a combination of migration from the mainland and a relatively high birth rate led to severe pressures to expand the capital of Lelanàn. In response, the powerful couple of Pydra Summerfoot, a high-ranking Sisterhood Priestess, and her husband Manaly, a prominent city merchant, proposed a particularly ambitious project - the construction of a new Anánoma, a traditional Vyzemby fortified settlement shaped like a beehive. Modern in style and function, the new Anánoma would allow the city’s continued expansion and raise the prestige and position of Lelanàn among the older and more established cities of the Vyzemby. The new Anánoma placed the temple of Lel in a position of prominence, and housed the residence of the Chosen of Lel herself. The Anánoma was built in such a way to make continued expansion easy and efficient - and continued to grow well after the deaths of the Summerfoots as did the city’s prestige and power.

  • Construction cost: -10% (build_cost; raw value -0.1).

4. Temples of Love

With the prominence of Lel and the temporal power of her sisterhood, temples devoted to her worship were the center of religious life within the bustling theocracy. While priestesses assumed many roles from providing medicine to distributing food and charity, Lel’s most sacred gifts lay in her domain over love and fertility. Those temples, designated "temples of love," specialized in sacred acts related to fertility, and were sought after by many of Lel’s devoted followers. The priestesses within were trained in ancient rites thought to enhance fertility, a favorite of couples seeking to expand their families, but also of love itself. Young prospective couples may seek the assistance of the temple priestess to help guide them to test their compatibility - and the arrival of a child would be seen as the clearest blessing by Lel of their union. Those seeking companionship also visited the temples on their own - and, if fortunate and devout, could help bolster the ranks of the faithful.

  • Manpower recovery speed: +15% (manpower_recovery_speed; raw value 0.15).

5. The Enahelibe Ritual

As a nexus of cultures across the isles and a flourishing city state, Lelanàn began to develop its own unique rituals and practices. Chief among these was the ritual dance of Enahelibe, a mostly slow, deliberate dance punctuated by moments of rapid movement and brief periods of improvisation. The Enahelibe first developed as a ritual by the priestesses of the temples of love, as a rite of fertility to summon Lel’s blessing. Most common at gatherings of younger halflings and weddings, the Enahelibe became closely associated with Lelanàn even as it began to spread to other areas of the Isles.

  • True faith tolerance: +2 (tolerance_own; raw value 2).

6. Charity After the Eruption

The eruption of the volcano Afomapobo brought great devastation to much of the Summer Isles, destroying many Vyzemby settlements and darkening the skies with a sickening ash. The Sisterhood and temples of Lel were quick to provide relief for those affected by the eruption however, distributing food to those whose crops were destroyed or starved of sunlight, and finding homes for those left homeless or orphaned by the destruction. The temples of love were temporarily opened to serve as a place to feed and house those fleeing the lands blighted by the eruption, as the whole of Lelanàn joined together to provide for their less fortunate brethren. These efforts greatly increased the prestige of the temple, and reinforced the faith of the people in the state and its divine mission.

  • War exhaustion: -0.03 (war_exhaustion; raw value -0.03).

7. Scent of the Holy Waters

As Lelanàn grew into a center of culture and commerce, so too did it become a center of fashion and beauty. The most famed beauty product was a perfume known as "Ixora," derived from a white jungle flower with an extremely pleasant odor. Growing in abundance in the Mboala jungle just to Lelanán’s south, the cosmopolitan city’s demand for its fragrance led to the birth of an industry of growers and cultivators, until Ixora became intrinsically linked with the state and the worship of Lel herself. This demand only grew exponentially when foreign noblewomen were exposed to Ixora perfume by Vyzemby traders, with Pearlsedger noblewomen in particular buying Ixora in great quantities. This craze saw a boom in trade, with Lelanán in particular benefiting from its association with the scent.

  • Trade efficiency: +10% (trade_efficiency; raw value 0.1).
